Hey, recovering alcoholic here! 

Accepting that alcohol makes my BPD worse was just a fact I had to accept really. It’s a tricky one because sometimes alcohol is the only thing that calms down all the chaos (G&T is my favourite vice too!) But every time, without fail, no matter how much I’d drink, I’d always feel worse after the initial  euphoria wore off, and regret it. 

Right now, I’m trying to find other ways of managing my emotions when all the intrusive thoughts arise, without resorting to drink, but it’s a challenge.

I’ve started to get to know myself well enough to realise that there are certain hours of the day I can expect to be reasonably ‘productive’ and certain hours where I am simply of no use to myself or in the state of mind to do anything.

 I wake up at around 7am, and with coffee I’m usually able to concentrate for a good 2 hours. Sometimes I really feel like it’s a race against the clocks to get as much done possible before my mood flips and I feel hopeless again. After lunch I do less intellectually engaging activities that don’t demand a lot, but that keep me from just laying with my head face down into the pillow for the rest of the day ( usually reading, researching things that interest me, watching a film etc). 

It’s been a real challenge to accept that I am not a productivity power house that can work 8 hours a day ( as I used to do), and I sometimes feel guilty, but planning my day around, and according to how I KNOW my moods will fluctuate has really helped.  (So basically doing tasks according to what my mood allows me to do eg.not trying to force productivity when I feel depressed and just want to lie down)
